tam.headline: The four Rio routes are the floor — Brazil's water-crossing market runs far higher

rungs.label: What the four Rio routes support today
rungs.note: Navier's annual revenue across the four sourced Rio cross-bay routes at full fleet (113 boats). This is the grounded floor, not the whole market.

rungs.label: Matured Brazil network Navier can serve
rungs.note: Navier's own transport revenue once the full addressable Brazilian network runs at leading-operator capture, with faster, more comfortable boats growing the market. Mid case shown with a low–high range.

rungs.label: Brazil marine-mobility opportunity
rungs.note: Total annual water-transfer spend the induced Brazilian crossing market can support at full network width.

rungs.label: Whole-journey value across those crossings
rungs.note: Door-to-door value of every journey that includes one of these crossings — the full trip, not only the boat leg.

rules.unit_economics_route: single representative exact-bound route; all values bound from the aggregate, never hand-typed
rules.tam_source: SOM floor from aggregate grounded_floor_by_market; SAM/marine-TAM/journey-GMV rungs from finance/model/growth.py LB-254 ladder on the Brazil pool (see tam.source)
rules.published_brazil_basis: shared unchanged across DiDi Brazil and inDrive Brazil (transport rungs 1-4)
rules.platform_take_rung: HELD for inDrive — inDrive's low/near-zero-commission model makes the standard 18% take-rate rung unsupportable; a whole-journey take rung is added only with inDrive's own sourced take rate (null-beats-guess)
